title: Connector Labs: All-Hands Prep + Exec Update (v0.1)
content:
Context and intent:

This doc captures a lightweight prep run for a compact all-hands + executive update we plan to run mid-Q2. Goal is to converge the leadership narrative, surface 6 operational asks (actionable, ownerable), and validate the OKR framing that product/eng/sales will use in town-level comms. Treat as working notes — lots of open questions flagged below.

High-level objectives for the session (what success looks like):
- One coherent 8-10 minute exec update (CEO + CTO) that ties northstar → customer evidence → 3 asks.
- Publish a short OKR draft (company + 3 cross-functional priorities) for Q3 that has measurable targets and owners.
- All-hands run-of-show rehearsed with clear escalation/fallback.
- Identify 4 dependency risks to surface to the board and mitigation owners.

Guiding hypotheses (for debate in the prep):
1) Tight narratives (metrics + 1 customer story) reduce post-town confusion and reduce follow-up questions by ~40%.
2) Focusing on two concrete platform levers (Dedicated capacity pricing and Optimize suggestions) will yield the highest immediate impact on GTM asks.
3) A short, actionable set of team asks with owners beats a longer aspirational deck at motivating cross-team follow-through.

Draft company OKRs (Q3) — early framing (numbers = starting point, needs calibration):
- Objective: Make inference economics predictable for mid-market customers
  - KR1: Reduce median hosted API tail-latency (p95) from 210ms → 150ms across top-5 endpoints
  - KR2: Decrease per-token hosted cost by 18% vs baseline (through batching + cache suggestions)
  - KR3: Win 6 Dedicated contracts (>= $25k/mo ACV) with SLA commitments
  - Owner: VP Customer Success + Head of Product (metric owners assigned)

- Objective: Increase product reliability and graceful degradation
  - KR1: Implement automated fallback routing for top-3 models in production (30-day beta)
  - KR2: Reduce customer-facing incidents impacting latency >500ms by 50% quarter-over-quarter
  - Owner: SRE + Serving Runtime Eng Lead

- Cross-functional priority: Simplify Private deployment onboarding (reduce time-to-first-run)
  - KR1: Deliver a VPC quickstart template and automation that reduces setup time from 7d → 2d for pilot customers
  - Owner: Private Deployments product manager + Platform Eng

All-hands run-of-show (compact 40 minute format) — roles and rough timing:
- 00:00–02:00 Opening (CEO) — appetite framing, one-line mission reminder, one customer snippet (ops team to sponsor video clip)
- 02:00–10:00 Exec update (CEO + CTO) — metrics, wins, top risks, 3 asks. One slide per ask (ask = what, why, owner, due date)
- 10:00–20:00 Product demo (2min highlight + 5 minute rapid demo of Optimize suggestions on a real workload, Q&A distributed to product desks)
- 20:00–30:00 Team spotlights (three 3min lightning updates: Dedicated ops, Private onboarding, Console observability)
- 30:00–36:00 Live Q&A (moderated by Head of Comms — collect Slack questions ahead to prune)
- 36:00–40:00 Close + immediate next steps (CTO recaps asks and owner names)

Rehearsal notes / constraints:
- Keep slides to max 12. Avoid deep technical dive in the exec update; include appendix for curious SREs/Eng.
- Require 1 full dress rehearsal with AV two business days before event. AV checklist attached in linked_artifacts.
- Fallback plan: If demo fails, default to recorded demo clip (backup owner: Maya Rivera).

Executive update bullet bank (draft talking points) — pick 3 strong ones:
- Customer evidence: Two pilot customers reported 25% faster inference on average after tuning quant profiles; Customer X testimonial snippet prepared (Noah to confirm legal ok).
- Financial lens: On-hosted API usage growth 24% QoQ; unit economics improving via batching—call out projected per-token cost delta.
- Risk callout: Capacity spike vulnerability in region-eu-west2 during scheduled infra maintenance; mitigation = auto-fallback to reserved capacity pool (SRE owner).

Decision log / open questions to resolve before rehearsal:
- Q1: Acceptable tightening of KR numbers? Product/Finance to confirm 4–6 business days before rehearsal (linked ticket: JIRA-OPS-1298).
- Q2: Which Dedicated contract wins can be called out as references? Sales to confirm NDA status.
- Q3: Who is the formal incident escalation owner for the fallback pool? (SRE to confirm on or before 2026-02-18).

Risks and mitigation (short list):
- Risk: Demo instability on large model due to GPU kernel mismatch. Mitigation: Ship a small synthetic demo that mirrors customer workflow + appendix with logs. Owner: Eng-Serving Runtime.
- Risk: Mixed messaging on private vs dedicated offerings (customers confused). Mitigation: One-page customer-facing table + single-line positioning for exec slide. Owner: Head of Product Marketing.
- Risk: Late legal clearance on customer quote. Mitigation: Prepare two alternate quotes (generic + specific). Owner: Legal contact: Priya Shah.

Action items (owners + dates) — first pass:
- Finalize OKR KR targets and owners (Owner: Sofia Patel, due 2026-02-18)
- Draft the 3 exec asks slide copy (Owner: Noah Chen, due 2026-02-22)
- Confirm customer quote permissions (Owner: Sales Ops, due 2026-02-19)
- Schedule full dress rehearsal + AV check (Owner: Maya Rivera, due 2026-02-25)
- Produce two demo fallbacks (recorded + synthetic) (Owner: Ethan Brooks, due 2026-02-24)

Notes-to-self / rough ideas to iterate on in next pass:
- Consider running a 15-minute pre-call for managers to align on how to cascade asks to teams (managers-only session).
- Add a one-slide micro-FAQ that answers expected questions about pricing and scaling.
- Explore a short survey (2 questions) after all-hands to measure clarity of asks (owner: People Ops).

Appendix (links + references):
- Confluence draft for Q3 OKRs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/connector-labs
- JIRA backlog: JIRA-OPS-1287, JIRA-OPS-1298
